decision_conditions:
Condition : 1 - The development hereby permitted shall be begun within 3 years from the date of this permission.
Reason: To prevent the accumulation of unimplemented planning permissions and to comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended) and to meet the requirements of Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004 and to meet the requirements of The Town and Country Planning (Development Management Procedure) (England) Order 2015.
Condition : 2 - The development shall be carried out in accordance with the reports, specifications and drawings detailed: 
PA-1110-MB-000-101, PA-1110-MB-000-100, PA-1110-MB-00-100 Rev. 02, PA-1110-MB-00-101 Rev.01, PA-1110-MB-00-102 Rev. 01, PA-1110-MB-04-100 Rev. 01, PA-1110-MB-04-103 Rev. 01, PA-1110-MB-04-101 Rev.01, PA-1110-MB-06-100, PA-1110-MB-04-102, PA-1110-MB-00-103 and Fire Planning Statement prepared by Fire Safety Engineering Consultancy (dated 11th March 2026, Issue No: 2) 
Reason: To ensure a satisfactory standard of development and to allow the local planning authority to review any potential changes to the scheme.

Condition : 3 - No development shall take place until full details of existing and proposed site levels shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details.
Reason: To ensure the development relates satisfactorily to its surroundings, and in accordance with Council policies LP1 and LP2 of the Local Plan coupled with the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework. It is necessary for the condition to be discharged prior to the commencement of works to ensure the ground levels across the development are compatible with adjoining sites before the site is cleared.
Condition : 4 - No development shall commence until a Construction and Environmental Management Plan (CEMP) has been submitted to and been approved in writing by the local planning authority. The CEMP shall include measures to mitigate the construction effects as part of a coordinated and collaborative approach with surrounding developments, and shall include the following details (although not limited to): 
a) whilst works should take place outside of the nesting season (March - August inclusive), if works to or near any trees, hedges and shrubs are unavoidable during this period, then a site walk over at least 48 hours prior to works commencing is required to check for any nesting birds. In the event that a nest is found, an appropriate exclusion zone should be implemented around it until the young have fully fledged (as stipulated by the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981 (as amended)). The law protects all wild bird species, their eggs and nests; 
b) whilst construction lighting should be avoided, if lighting is necessary, details of a construction lighting plan outlining how lighting will be prevented from negatively impacting any protected and priority species during construction, in particular commuting bats or adjacent habitats. This construction lighting plan should follow the best practice industry guidance outlined in the Bat Conservation Trust (BCT) and Institute of Lighting Professionals (ILP) Artificial Lighting Guidance Note (2023);
c) details of measures to prevent entrapment of or harm to wildlife on site, including in excavations and construction and waste materials left on site;
The demolition and construction works shall be carried out in full accordance with approved Construction and Environmental Management Plan (CEMP).
Reason: To ensure construction works and traffic impacts are minimised, to protect biodiversity and to mitigate the impacts of development on protected species in accordance with Council policies LP1, LP2, LP55 and LP56 of the Local Plan.
Condition : 5 - Prior to the commencement of above ground works, details and samples of materials proposed to be used on all external surfaces of the development (including balconies and terraces) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved materials and thereafter so retained.
Reason: In order to assess the suitability of the proposed materials, in the interests of the appearance of the locality and to preserve the setting of adjacent Listed Buildings, in accordance with Council policies LP1, LP2 and LP3 of the Local Plan coupled with the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework.
Condition : 6 - Prior to the commencement of above ground works, details of the height, design and materials of the proposed boundary treatment shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The boundary treatment shall be installed in accordance with the approved details prior to the first occupation of the development and shall be retained thereafter. 
Reason: To ensure a satisfactory appearance of the development and to protect visual amenities, in accordance with policies LP1 and LP2 of the Local Plan coupled with the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework.
Condition : 7 - The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the recommendations, tree protection measures and arboricultural supervision details set out within the Arboricultural Impact Report prepared by EnviroArb Solutions Ltd (dated 17th February 2026, Ref: EAS-163.2026). All tree protection measures shall be installed prior to the commencement of any works on site and shall be retained for the duration of the construction period. 
Reason: To preserve trees  of visual amenity and the character of the area, in accordance with Council policy LP56 of the Local Plan coupled with the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework.
Condition : 8 - Notwithstanding the details shown on the approved plans and set out in the supporting information, details of landscaping and ecological enhancements shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority prior to the commencement of any above ground works. The details shall include as a minimum:
1. Details of planting including species and plans, with priority given to wildlife friendly species;
2. Details of all biodiverse roofs (including any Biosolar roofs) including details of the substrate, features to be included within the substrate such as logs piles, sand/gravel piles and ephemeral water bodies etc., and details of any seeding/plug plant choice with priority given to wildflower and wildlife friendly species (in accordance with The Gro Green Roof Code 2021);
3. Details of at least 3 x bat bricks/boxes;
4. Details of at least 2 x bird bricks/boxes;
5. Details of invertebrate provision, with features located in warm, sheltered location near planting; 
6. Details of hedgehog holes within boundary treatment where appropriate;
7. If lighting is proposed, a bat sensitive post-construction lighting plan, to ensure that any lighting will be of a specification that minimises its impacts on bats and onsite and adjacent habitats in accordance with the BCT and ILP 2023 Guidance Note (including having a colour temperature of <2700k, no uplighters and no light spill onto sensitive habitats).
8. Details of a management plan to be implemented for the hard and soft landscaped areas.
The approved details shall be implemented in full prior to first occupation of the development and thereafter retained and maintained as such unless otherwise agreed by the local planning authority.
Reason: To ensure a satisfactory appearance and biodiversity value in the development, in accordance with Council policies LP1, LP55 and LP56 of the Local Plan. 
Condition : 9 - No development shall take place until; (A) i) a preliminary risk-assessment shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. ii) a site-investigation has been conducted to consider the potential for contaminated-land and shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. iii) a remediation method statement, described to make the site suitable for, intended use by removing unacceptable risks to sensitive receptors, and shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. (B) The remediation shall be completed then a verification report produced, and then that submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.
Reason: To ensure that risks from land contamination to the future users of the land and neighbouring land are minimised, together with those to controlled waters, property and ecological systems, and to ensure that the development can be carried out safely without unacceptable risks to workers, neighbours and other off-site receptors, having regard to Council policy LP14 of the Local Plan, coupled with the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework. The details are required prior to the start of the works so that the necessary precautions and mitigation measures can be incorporated into the excavation and construction.
Condition : 10 - No development shall commence, excluding demolition, site clearance, site investigations and remediation works, until a detailed surface water drainage scheme has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, in consultation with the Lead Local Flood Authority. The scheme shall include: 
a) Detailed drainage drawings and supporting calculations 
b) The results of infiltration testing and borehole investigations or, where infiltration drainage is demonstrated not to be feasible, evidence justifying an alternative drainage strategy
c) A completed SuDS Proforma; and
d) A management and maintenance plan confirming routine maintenance responsibilities and procedures for all drainage components for the lifetime of the development. 
The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved details. 
Reason: To ensure satisfactory sustainable drainage and to reduce the risk of flooding to and from the site, in accordance with Policy SI13 of the London Plan, Policy LP12 of the Wandsworth Local Plan (2023), the Non-Statutory Technical Standards for Sustainable Drainage Systems and the National Planning Policy Framework. 
Condition : 11 - Prior to the first occupation of the development, evidence demonstrating that the approved sustainable drainage scheme has been completed in accordance with the approved details shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The evidence shall include photographs of the installed drainage infrastructure and installation records or contractor certification, as appropriate. 
Reason: To ensure that the approved sustainable drainage system has been implemented and will continue to operate for the lifetime of the development, in accordance with Policy SI13 of the London Plan, Policy LP12 of the Wandsworth Local Plan (2023), the Non-Statutory Technical Standards for Sustainable Drainage Systems and the National Planning Policy Framework. 
Condition : 12 - Prior to the commencement of above ground works, details of the sound insulation measures to be incorporated into the development, including glazing, ventilation and any other mitigation necessary to protect future occupiers from externally generated noise including road, rail and aircraft, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
The details shall demonstrate that the development will achieve internal ambient noise levels that do not exceed the guideline values set out in Table 4 of BS 8233:2014 Guidance on Sound Insulation and Noise Reduction for Buildings. Where the required internal noise levels cannot be achieved with windows open, an appropriate alternative means of ventilation shall be provided. 
The approved mitigation measures shall be installed prior to first occupation of the development and shall thereafter be retained and maintained. 
Reason: To ensure an acceptable standard of residential amenity for future occupiers, in accordance with Council policies LP2 and LP14 of the Local Plan coupled with the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework.
Condition : 13 - Prior to the commencement of above ground works, details of a scheme for the sound insulation of the separating floor between the approved ground floor community facility (Use Class F2(b)) and the residential units above shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. 
The approved sound insulation measures shall be fully installed prior to the first occupation of the residential units and the commencement of the community use and shall thereafter be retained and maintained. No alteration shall be made to the separating floor or ceiling construction that would compromise the approved acoustic insulation without the prior written approval of the Local Planning Authority. 
Reason: To safeguard the amenities of future residential occupiers and users of the community facility, in accordance with Council policies LP2 and LP14 of the Local Plan coupled with the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework.
Condition : 14 - The development hereby approved shall achieve a minimum of a 35% reduction in CO2 emissions above the levels set in Building Regulations Part L 2021, with a site wide target of 66% as indicated within the Energy and Sustainability Statement prepared by Doherty Energy (dated 11th March 2026, Ref: E1568-ESS-01).Prior to first occupation of the development, evidence (e.g. photographs, copies of installation contracts and as-built worksheets prepared under SAP) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority, to demonstrate that the development has achieved at least a 35% reduction in CO2 emissions above the levels set in Building Regulations Part L 2021. The installed measures shall be retained in accordance with the approved details unless otherwise agreed by the local planning authority. 
Reason: In the interest of sustainable development and to accord with Council policy LP10 of the Local Plan coupled with the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework.
Condition : 15 - The development shall achieve a maximum water use of 110 litres per person per day for homes, in line with the Water Efficiency Calculator for new dwellings from the Department of Communities and Local Government. Prior to first occupation, evidence to demonstrate that that the internal water consumption of the development will not exceed 105/p/day must be submitted to the local planning authority and approved in writing, unless otherwise agreed in waiting by the local planning authority. Measures integrated shall be retained for the lifetime of the development.
Reason: In the interest of sustainable development and to accord with Council policy LP10 of the Local Plan coupled with the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework.
Condition : 16 - Prior to the commencement of above ground works, details of the appearance, location, orientation, total area and predicted carbon savings from the photovoltaic panels shall be submitted to and approved by the local planning authority to show how the renewable energy carbon savings are to be achieved. The photovoltaic panels shall be installed in accordance with the approved details prior to the occupation of the development, and retained and maintained as such unless otherwise agreed by the local planning authority. 
Reason: To achieve an appropriate appearance and sustainability standards in accordance with Council policies LP1 and LP10 of the Local Plan, coupled with the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework. 
Condition : 17 - Prior to the commencement of above ground works, and notwithstanding the approved drawings, details of the appearance, location, specification, predicted carbon savings (where applicable), predicated operational noise levels and any noise and vibration mitigation measures for all fixed plant and machinery, including the air source heat pump, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The submitted details shall demonstrate how the approved renewable energy carbon savings are to be achieved and shall include a noise control scheme demonstrating that the cumulative measured or calculated rating level of noise emitted from the fixed plants and machinery shall be at least 10dB(A) below the existing background noise level, when assessed in accordance with the latest version of British Standard 4142, at all times that the plant and machinery equipment are in operation. The rating level shall be determined at the boundary of the nearest ground floor noise sensitive premises or at a point 1 metre from the fa�ade of the nearest first floor (or higher) noise sensitive premises. Where an alternative assessment position is used due to access constraints, this shall be identified and supported by a location plan and noise propagation calculations demonstrating compliance with the required noise criterion. The approved scheme shall be implemented in full prior to the first operation of the plant and machinery and shall thereafter be retained and maintained for the lifetime of the development.  
Reason: To secure the approved renewable energy strategy, and to safeguard the amenities of neighbouring occupiers from noise associated with fixed plant and machinery, in accordance with Council policies LP2, LP10 and LP14 of the Local Plan coupled with the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework.
Condition : 18 - Prior to the commencement of above ground works, a BREEAM New Construction Design Stage Assessment, prepared by a licensed BREEAM Assessor, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The assessment shall demonstrate that the replacement community facility is designed to achieve a BREEAM 'Outstanding' rating. Where the assessment demonstrate, to the satisfaction of the local planning authority, that achieving an 'Outstanding' rating is not technically feasible, the assessment shall demonstrate the development is designed to achieve a minimum BREEAM 'Very Good' rating. The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved assessment. 
Reason: To achieve appropriate sustainability standards in accordance with Council policy LP10 of the Local Plan coupled with the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework.
Condition : 19 - Within three months of the first occupation of the community facility, a BREEAM New Construction Post-Construction Certificate, issued by the BRE (or equivalent accredited body), shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The certificate shall demonstrate that the development has achieved the rating approved pursuant to Condition 18. The approved sustainability measures shall thereafter be retained for the lifetime of the development. 
Reason: To achieve appropriate sustainability standards in accordance with Council policy LP10 of the Local Plan coupled with the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework.
Condition : 20 - Prior to the first occupation of the development, details of the cycle parking facilities shown on drawing number PA-1110-MB-00-100 Rev. 02 shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall include the specification of the proposed cycle stand, including their design, dimensions, materials and layout, for the provision of 11 long-stay residential cycle parking spaces (including 1 adaptable cycle parking space); 2 short-stay residential cycle parking spaces; 1 long-stay community cycle parking space; and 2 short-stay community cycle parking spaces. The cycle parking facilities shall be provided in accordance with the approved details prior to the first occupation of the development and shall thereafter be retained and kept available for cycle parking for the lifetime of the development. 
Reason: To ensure adequate provision is made for cycle parking in accordance with Council policies LP50 and LP51 of the Local Plan, Policy T5 of the London Plan coupled with the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework.
Condition : 21 - Prior to the first occupation of the development, the refuse and recycling storage facilities shown on approved drawing number PA-1110-MB-00-100 Rev. 02 shall be provided and made available for use. The approved refuse and recycling storage facilities shall thereafter be retained and kept available for the users of the development and for no other purposes. 
Reason: To ensure adequate provision is made for waste storage in accordance with Council policies LP1 and LP2 of the Local Plan coupled with the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework.
Condition : 22 - Prior to first occupation of the development hereby approved, all ground, first and second floor windows and glazed openings within the northern and southern side elevations (excluding the windows and glazed openings serving the kitchen/living/dining room of Units 02 and 06 and Bedroom 01 of Unit 06), and as shown on drawing numbers PA-1110-MB-00-100 Rev. 02, PA-1110-MB-00-101 Rev.01 , PA-1110-MB-00-102 Rev. 01, PA-1110-MB-04-103  Rev.01 and PA-1110-MB-04-101 Rev.01, shall be fitted with obscure glazing to a minimum of Level 3 on the Pilkington scale (or equivalent) up to a height of 1.7 metres above the internal finished floor level and shall be non-opening below this level. The obscure glazing shall thereafter be permanently retained. 
Reason: To protect neighbouring amenities and to safeguard the future redevelopment potential of neighbouring sites, in accordance with Council policies LP1 and LP2 of the Wandsworth Local Plan coupled with the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework.
Condition : 23 - With the exception of the approved ground floor terrace and first and second floor balconies shown on drawings numbers PA-1110-MB-00-100 Rev. 02, PA-1110-MB-00-101 Rev.01 and PA-1110-MB-00-102 Rev. 01, no part of the roof of the development hereby permitted shall be used as a balcony, roof terrace, roof garden or other external amenity area. No balustrades, railings, means of enclosure or means of permanent access shall be erected or installed on any part of the roof not expressly approved for such use. 
Reason: To protect the amenities of neighbouring occupiers by preventing overlooking, loss of privacy and noise disturbance, in accordance with Council policies LP1 and LP2 of the Local Plan coupled with the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework.
Condition : 24 - Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (as amended), or any Order revoking and re-enacting that Order, the approved community floorspace shown on drawing number PA-1110-MB-00-100 Rev. 02 shall be used only as a community hall or meeting place for the principal use of the local community (Use Class F2(b)) and for no other purpose, including any other use within Class F of the Schedule to the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 (as amended), or any equivalent provision in any statutory instrument revoking and re-enacting that Order. 
Reason: To safeguard the amenities of neighbouring occupiers and to ensure the replacement community floorspace remains available to meet local community needs, in accordance with Policies LP2 and LP17 of the Wandsworth Local Plan (2023) and the National Planning Policy Framework.
Condition : 25 - Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (or any Order revoking, amending or re-enacting that Order) no satellite dishes, telecommunications masts, antennas or equipment or associated structures, shall be installed on the external elevations or roof of the building hereby approved.
Reason: To protect the appearance of the building, and accord with Council policies LP1, LP2 and LP22 of the Local Plan coupled with the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework.
Condition : 26 - No pipes or flues, other than rainwater pipes, shall be installed on the front elevation of the building hereby approved.
Reason: To safeguard the appearance of the area, in accordance with Council Policy LP1 of the Local Plan coupled with the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework.
Condition : 27 - Prior to the commencement of the community facility, a Maintenance and Funding Plan for the community facility shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The plan shall demonstrate:
a) That sufficient funding has been secured to provide for the ongoing maintenance of the community facility
b) That service charges associated with the operation and maintenance of the community facility will be affordable
The community facility shall thereafter be managed and maintained in accordance with the approved Maintenance and Funding Plan for the lifetime of the development. 
Reason: To ensure the viability and longevity of the proposed community use in accordance with Council policy LP17 of the Local Plan coupled with the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework.
Condition : 28 - Notwithstanding the detail shown on the approved drawings, prior to the first use of the first and second floor balconies, details of privacy screening to the northern boundaries of the private balconies of Units 05 and 08 and the southern boundaries of the private balconies of Units 02 and 06 (as shown on approved drawing numbers PA-1110-MB-00-101 Rev.01,PA-1110-MB-00-102 Rev. 01, PA-1110-MB-04-103 Rev. 01 and  PA-1110-MB-04-101 Rev. 01) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The details shall include a minimum height of 1.7 metres above finished floor level, design, appearance and materials. The approved screening shall be installed in accordance with the approved details prior to the first use of the balconies and shall thereafter be permanently retained and maintained. 
Reason: To safeguard the future redevelopment potential of adjoining sites and in the interest of visual amenities in accordance with Council policies LP1 and LP2 of the Local Plan coupled with the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework.
Condition : 29 - No development, including any demolition, shall take place until a construction management plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The construction management plan shall include details (but not limited to) of the routing of construction vehicles, time of arrival and departure, and any proposed temporary traffic and pedestrian management measures during the course of construction. The demolition and construction works shall be carried out in accordance with the approved plan. 
Reason: In the interests of traffic, general amenity of the area and neighbour amenity in accordance with Council policy LP50 and LP51 of the Local Plan coupled with the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework. It is necessary for the condition to be discharged prior to the commencement of any works on site to ensure the whole construction phase is in accordance with an approved plan.
Condition : 30 - Prior to first occupation, a Refuse Management Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Plan shall include details: 
a) Confirming that the communal refuse and recycling bins serving the residential units will be accessible to the Council's refuse collection service via a Fire Brigade FB2 or FB4 key, or an equivalent access mechanism agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority.
b) Frequency, servicing arrangements and management of waste arising from the community facility. 
The development shall thereafter operate in accordance with the approved Refuse Management Plan for the lifetime of the development. 
Reason: To ensure appropriate and secure access for waste collection services and to safeguard residential amenity and public health, in accordance with Policies LP1 and LP2 of the Local Plan coupled with the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework.
Condition : 31 - The community premises hereby permitted shall not be open other than between the 
hours of: 
(a) 08:00 - 19:00 Mondays - Fridays  
(b) 09:00 - 23:00 Saturdays   
(c) 09:00 - 17:00 Sundays 
Reason: To safeguard the amenities of the neighbourhood, in accordance with  Council policy LP2 of the Local Plan coupled with the requirements of the National  Planning Policy Framework.
Condition : 32 - INFORMATIVE: In dealing with this application the Council has implemented the requirement in the National Planning Policy Framework to work with the applicant in a positive and proactive manner and the Council has, as far as practicable, sought solutions to problems arising in relation to dealing with the planning application. The Council has made available detailed advice in the form of its statutory policies in the Local Plan (2023) as well as offering a full pre-application advice service, in order to ensure that the applicant has been given every opportunity to submit an application which is likely to be considered favourably. In addition, where appropriate, further guidance was offered to the applicant during the processing of the application.
Condition : 33 - INFORMATIVE: Community Infrastructure Levy (CIL): From the information available, it appears that the development permitted is subject to a Community Infrastructure Levy charge in accordance with the Community Infrastructure Levy Regulations 2010 (as amended). Any assessment of CIL liability by the Council has been based on the information provided and is not intended to provide a binding estimate of the actual CIL liability likely to be incurred.  General information on the Community Infrastructure Levy, including the forms that should be submitted to the Council can be found on the Council�s website.
description: Demolition of existing building and erection of a part two-storey part three-storey building to provide 1x Studio, 2 x 1 bedroom, 4x 2 bedroom and 1 x 3 bedroom flats (Class C3) with balconies and the use of part ground floor as a community use (Class F2).
